articles.body: Meta-Ability: "Tests All Green" Only Counts After You Replay It Source version of CodeSmith : v0.5.0 (commit 3a74c82f ). All paths are relative to the repo root; line numbers refer to this version. Intended audience: anyone who has been handed an agent's report that "all the tests passed," then watched everything turn red the moment they ran the tests themselves. When the model says "tests all green," what are those words worth? v0.5.0's answer: at the instant a turn ends and the model has just finished saying it, the engine replays, exactly as-is, the verification commands the model itself ran that turn, and reconciles the books against the exit codes. The verdict is written back into the conversation as a four-tuple, on by default, in a module of 914 lines.

articles.excerpt: YuE2: How Symbolic Planning Brings Transparency and Control to AI Music Generation Music generation models have made rapid progress, but most treat composition as a black box: you provide a text promp…
articles.body: YuE2: How Symbolic Planning Brings Transparency and Control to AI Music Generation Music generation models have made rapid progress, but most treat composition as a black box: you provide a text prompt, and audio emerges from a dense neural process that no one—including the model—can inspect or edit mid-flight. YuE2, introduced in a technical report from the multimodal-art-projection team published in late September 2026, takes a different approach. It generates a readable musical score first, then renders that score into audio. The result is a system that is both more controllable and, according to expert listening evaluations, more musical.

articles.title: Fixing iPhone HEVC for Telegram Video Avatars with ffmpeg
articles.excerpt: The Problem I wanted to set a short video clip as my Telegram profile avatar. Telegram lets you do that. Upload an MP4, it trims to 10 seconds, done. Except it doesn't always work. Drag in a clip reco…
articles.body: The Problem I wanted to set a short video clip as my Telegram profile avatar. Telegram lets you do that. Upload an MP4, it trims to 10 seconds, done. Except it doesn't always work. Drag in a clip recorded on an iPhone and Telegram just silently does nothing. No error, no feedback. The avatar doesn't change. The issue is HEVC (H.265). iPhones have been shooting HEVC by default since iOS 11. Telegram's video avatar processor only accepts H.264. It rejects HEVC files without telling you why. So I built a bot to handle it: @LiveAvaBot . Send it any video or GIF, get back a ready-to-upload avatar file. Here's what I learned building it. What Telegram Actually Requires The official docs are thin on details.
articles.author: liveavabot

articles.title: I built a desktop widget that turns my Claude Code, Codex and Cursor limits into a pixel hero's HP
articles.excerpt: I switch between Claude Code, Codex and Cursor all day, and I got tired of checking how much of each limit I had left. Every check meant going to a different place for each tool, and I was doing it ov…
articles.body: I switch between Claude Code, Codex and Cursor all day, and I got tired of checking how much of each limit I had left. Every check meant going to a different place for each tool, and I was doing it over and over just to decide which agent to use next. So I built Token Slayer , a small always-on-top desktop widget. Each service gets a pixel hero. Remaining usage is the hero's HP. When an agent is working, the hero fights. When it's idle, the hero rests by a campfire. What it does HP = remaining usage for Claude Code (5-hour and weekly), Codex (5-hour and weekly) and Cursor (monthly). Fights while your agent works. It watches local activity, so the hero reacts within a few seconds of a new turn. Runway prediction. From the last 30 minutes of use, it estimates when you'll hit 0%.

Ridley Scott and Drew Goddard’s adaptation of Weir’s story of an astronaut methodically growing potatoes on Mars is a masterpiece, filled with optimism, humor, and thrills. articles.title: Life after the moon: Artemis II's Christina Koch steps down from active astronaut duty
articles.excerpt: Artemis II mission specialist Christina Koch will become NASA's acting deputy chief engineer on Nov. 1. All four Artemis II crewmates have now stepped away from active spaceflight duties.
articles.body: Don't expect any of the Artemis II moon astronauts to fly again soon. On Tuesday (Oct. 13), NASA announced that Artemis II mission specialist Christina Koch will become the agency’s acting deputy chief engineer, effective Nov. 1. "With this appointment, Koch will transition to management astronaut status and will no longer be eligible for future spaceflight assignments," NASA officials wrote in a statement on Tuesday . Her three Artemis II crewmates had already shared their next moves, none of which put another spaceflight in play in the near future. Mission commander Reid Wiseman and pilot Victor Glover , both of NASA, became "emeritus" astronauts last month, a role that seems to include planning, advising and mentoring duties but no flights into the final frontier.

articles.title: Anthropic warns small AI models could self-replicate through IoT devices
articles.excerpt: "Small weight-based replicators" could usher in a new generation of computer worms.
articles.body: AI company Anthropic is warning that advances in small AI models could soon usher in a new era of self-replicating malware that’s capable of infecting smart fridges, vacuum cleaners, and a wide range of other Internet-of-things devices and is more resistant to takedown. By next year, smaller AI models may be able to autonomously self-replicate on all kinds of IoT devices, the company said. Eventually, the capability could enable computer worms, which propagate without requiring human interaction and are capable of infecting unfamiliar IoT devices. An experiment the company performed recently revealed significant challenges in bringing such an AI malware replicator to fruition, so the finding is necessarily tempered.
